newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Health Council adopts texts on blood, TSEs.
newsitem.headline: Health Council adopts texts on blood, TSEs.

text.p: The Health Council adopted texts on Tuesday on blood safety, EU health policies and diseases known as TSEs.
It also adopted a resolution on smoking (see BC-HEALTH-SMOKING) and debated proposals to set up an EU monitoring network for communicable diseases and create a European Health Card.

BLOOD SAFETY. The Council adopted a resolution urging EU states to examine their procedures and programmes for guaranteeing the safety of transfusion blood in light of recommendations outlined by a group of experts who met in Adare, Ireland, in September.
The resolution asks the Commission to present urgent proposals to support a coordinated approach to the question.

The experts in Adare highlighted the need to promote common measures for selecting blood donors and treating blood to assure confidence in transfusions and to promote EU self-sufficiency in blood supplies.

TSEs. The Council adopted conclusions asking EU states to step up coordination to prevent the spread of Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathies (TSEs) -- such as mad cow disease -- to humans. They called on all EU states to participate in a network for monitoring Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, the human equivalent of mad cow disease.
It said the EU must coordinate the work of all bodies concerned with TSEs, including Commission comittees, and promote research to combat the diseases.

HEALTH POLICIES. The Council adopted a resolution asking the Commission to draw up criteria and methods for incorporating health protection requirements into EU policy areas such as social policy, internal market, agriculture, food and fisheries, research and development, environment and energy, transport and international cooperation.

COMMUNICABLE DISEASES. The Council held an orientation debate on a draft decision, COM(96)789, to set up an EU network for monitoring and controlling communicable diseases. However, it sent it back to COREPER, the EU Committee of Permanent Representatives, to try to resolve conflicts over questions such as the legal base, subsidiarity and financing, an EU official said.

EUROPEAN HEALTH CARD. The Council discussed the possibility of introducing an electronic European Health Card carrying information about an individual's health in case of emergency. The ministers agreed the time was not yet ripe to make such a move because of the technical complexity, but that the Commission should support scientific research in the area, an EU official said.
